rows.title: Nuclear power is officially a clean energy source in Colorado. Not everyone is pleased.
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1040, signed into law Monday, adds to the state’s options to meet its emission reduction goals. Opponents criticized the state for ignoring nuclear’s toxic legacy.

rows.title: Colorado utility bills could rise, emissions cuts would be slowed if Trump ends clean energy tax credits
rows.standfirst: GOP Reps. Gabe Evans and Jeff Hurd have joined the fight to protect the federal energy tax credits behind $3.7B in projects and investments in their congressional districts

rows.title: Future of union organizing in Colorado remains fuzzy as legislative session enters home stretch
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 5 would abolish a requirement in the Colorado Labor Peace Act that 75% of workers at a company sign off before union security negotiations can begin. The bill is a priority for unions and loathed by business interests. Gov. Jared Polis is in the mix, too.

rows.title: Trump administration releases $3.2B in federal funds for Colorado’s electric co-ops. There may be a catch.
rows.standfirst: Funds granted under Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act have been transferred, but come with an option to modify plans to fit President Trump’s “Unleashing American Energy” executive order

rows.title: Colorado’s marijuana tax revenue keeps falling from its pandemic high, spurring new calls to rein in spending
rows.standfirst: As of last year, marijuana tax collections had declined about 41% from their pandemic peak, falling to $252 million from $424 million. Now state budget writers are calling for a line-by-line review of the Marijuana Tax Cash Fund.

rows.title: Coloradans rushed to buy cars before wave of Trump tariffs take effect
rows.standfirst: Colorado auto dealers had a busy weekend as customers scrambled to get a vehicle before the president’s 25% tariff on car imports — and all the reciprocal tariffs — cause prices to jump

rows.title: Was Colorado one of the fastest-growing economies in the US in 2024?
rows.standfirst: No. After a period of solid growth, Colorado’s ranking in a key economic indicator tumbled in 2024.

rows.title: Trump planning to use NREL land near Boulder for private AI data center and power plant, building on prior Biden order
rows.standfirst: The plan for 16 sites similar to the National Renewable Energy Lab could lend computing power to researchers as the U.S. looks to be competitive in the AI race

rows.title: What’s Working: Though expected, tariffs shocked Colorado business leaders to third-worst outlook in 23 years
rows.standfirst: Even a computer maker that moved manufacturing to Denver years ago isn’t immune. Plus: Updates on condos, quantum, broadband and more

rows.title: Thousands show up across Colorado to say “Hands Off!” to Trump administration
rows.standfirst: People in towns and cities, large and small, spoke up on Saturday afternoon, airing a list of grievances as diverse as the state itself

rows.title: Colorado utilities are trying to go green. Tariffs and geopolitical chaos are getting in the way.
rows.standfirst: In the middle of it all, the Colorado Energy Office and Gov. Jared Polis tested the waters for a bill that would move up clean-power goals by a decade

rows.title: Could a small southern Colorado town’s tech hub be replicated in other rural communities?
rows.standfirst: Since opening in 2019, Emergent Campus Florence has filled the classrooms of an old school with 18 businesses and 120 employees. The economic impact of new tech jobs in the region is adding up.

rows.title: Colorado ditches plan to trade utilities’ wildfire liability for insurance funding. Homeowners may foot bill instead.
rows.standfirst: A 0.5% fee would be imposed under House Bill 1302 on every home insurance policy in Colorado unless a house meets certain wildfire mitigation standards

rows.title: How Colorado’s business community is dealing with on-again, off-again tariffs
rows.standfirst: With reciprocal tariffs of up to 50% kicking in before getting paused by the Trump administration, local companies just want some certainty

rows.title: Support for Trump among Colorado Republicans remains overwhelming, even if they’re uneasy about economy
rows.standfirst: A recent poll revealed that 87% of registered GOP voters in Colorado had a favorable opinion of Trump at the end of March, though 61% felt the current state of the economy was fair or poor

rows.title: Colorado governor signs bill halting expansion of hard liquor sales in grocery and big-box stores
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 33 was brought as a way to protect small businesses that sell alcohol from further economic decline following the expansion of beer and wine sales in grocery stores. Supporters worried Gov. Jared Polis would veto it.

rows.title: What’s Working: More Colorado houses hit the market, but they’re also sitting around longer
rows.standfirst: The for-sale housing market is not back to normal yet. And then there’s condos. Plus: Tariffs’ impact on Colorado, a job fair with a $500 bonus, and more!

rows.title: Lawsuit attacking Colorado oil and gas rules echoes Trump’s push to roll back local green laws
rows.standfirst: Western Slope trade group seeks to overturn new state limits on pipeline emissions, while Trump urges his DOJ to roll back “ideologically motivated” policies

rows.title: Colorado won’t become latest state requiring porn sites to verify their users’ age after lawmakers abandon bill
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 201 would have required pornographic websites that are accessible in Colorado check to make sure their users are of age either through government-issued ID or artificial intelligence examination of user photos

rows.title: Colorado doubles down on quantum technology despite federal funding questions
rows.standfirst: On World Quantum Day, Gov. Polis and the state Department of Education rolled out a blueprint to build a quantum workforce as local companies look toward the future

rows.title: Coal-fired power plant in northwestern Colorado still set for 2028 closure despite Trump administration orders
rows.standfirst: Tri-State Generation is reviewing executive orders, but says its plan to close all three coal-fired units at Craig Station is based on economics

rows.title: Review of decision not to award Space Command to Alabama inconclusive, with Trump reversal expected
rows.standfirst: The location of U.S. Space Command, currently headquartered in Colorado Springs, has significant implications for the local economy, given the fast growth in national defense spending in space-based communications and defenses

rows.title: Legislature passes bill letting Colorado counties ask voters to triple lodging tax to 6%
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers say the measure is intended to help counties diversify their revenue streams, particularly in rural resort areas trying to fulfill a host of community needs like improving local roads and providing more affordable housing

rows.title: Colorado legislature passes bill punting to local governments on how much restaurant servers are paid
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1208, which passed the legislature and is awaiting Gov. Jared Polis’ signature, would let local governments where the minimum wage is higher than the state’s minimum decide how to calculate the base pay of tipped workers

rows.title: A dip in Colorado electric vehicle sales doesn’t have car dealers panicking — yet
rows.standfirst: The politics embroiling Tesla and stale models hurt sales for the top EV brand, but a $7,500 federal subsidy is still in place and hybrids are proving a popular choice for consumers

rows.title: What’s Working: Trump told farmers and ranchers to “have fun” with his cuts and tariffs. They aren’t.
rows.standfirst: Canceled grants hurt Colorado’s climate-smart farming organizations. Plus: Colorado lost jobs in March as jobless grew to 4.8%, King Soopers union sues, Denver permits speed up, and more!

rows.title: The women’s soccer stadium in Kansas City has been a big economic success. Can Denver replicate that?
rows.standfirst: CPKC Stadium, America’s first women’s sports venue, has broken ticket records and launched a development boom in KC. Denver’s City Council isn’t sold on helping to fund a sequel.

rows.title: Veto showdown looms for bill regulating social media sites in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Backers want platforms to have to take action when users engage in illegal activity, but Gov. Jared Polis has serious concerns about the policy

rows.title: Why Colorado’s artificial intelligence law is a big deal for the whole country
rows.standfirst: Nearly a year after it passed, it’s still the only one of its kind, so far. But as revisions are still planned, could Colorado’s law become a model to emulate — or avoid?

rows.title: Colorado could become first state to require climate change warning for gasoline sales
rows.standfirst: Like labels on cigarettes, opponents say fossil fuel warnings could change attitudes. Others call it “gasoline shaming.”

rows.title: With billions at stake, Colorado joins multi-state lawsuit to block Trump tariffs
rows.standfirst: Bipartisan lawsuit says president-initiated tariffs are unconstitutional. Trump administration is considering lowering tariffs on China

rows.title: As state lawmakers mull tax breaks for tech giants, critics wonder: What’s in it for Coloradans?
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 280 would exempt data centers from state sales taxes to attract jobs to Colorado. Other states show there are costly trade-offs.

rows.title: Colorado drillers must recycle fracking water starting in 2026 under first-in-the-nation rules
rows.standfirst: Front Range oil and gas development uses more fresh water in a year than the city of Boulder consumes. The state wants at least some of that to be recycled.

rows.title: Jared Polis’ plan to accelerate Colorado’s clean energy transition won’t reach the legislature this year
rows.standfirst: If enacted, the plan would have required Colorado’s investor-owned utilities — Xcel Energy and Black Hills Energy — to eliminate climate-warming emissions associated with electricity production by 2040, a decade sooner than currently required under state law

rows.title: Jared Polis vetoes bill regulating social media sites operating in Colorado; lawmakers signal override fight is coming
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 86 would require large social media companies used by people in Colorado to take down flagged accounts if they’re determined to be selling guns or drugs, or if the accounts are engaged in the sex trafficking or sexual exploitation of minors.

rows.title: Colorado’s Medicaid program now covers doula services
rows.standfirst: Most insurers do not cover doulas as a standard benefit. But in July, Colorado’s Medicaid program added doulas as a covered benefit.

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers move to ban sexually exploitative images, video created with artificial intelligence
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 288 would expand Colorado’s existing laws around posting intimate images to include material created by AI

rows.title: Colorado Senate overrides Jared Polis’ veto of bill regulating social media in extremely rare rebuke of governor
rows.standfirst: The last veto overrides in Colorado were in 2011 and 2007 under former Democratic Govs. John Hickenlooper and Bill Ritter, and both dealt with budget spending requests.

rows.title: What’s Working: Why rents in Denver and other parts of Colorado are dropping
rows.standfirst: So many new apartments hit the metro Denver market last year. Too many? Plus: Not every place has seen rents drop.

rows.title: Magic mushrooms aren’t the only fungi growing in Colorado. Meet the gourmet “weirdos.”
rows.standfirst: While psychedelics grab the headlines, interest in edible mushrooms is also peaking. With at least 100 varieties grown in Colorado and millions around the world, it’s boom times for fungi enthusiasts.

rows.title: Is transportation a top household expense in the US?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Transportation is the second-highest expense for households nationwide, behind housing costs, Bureau of Labor Statistics data shows.

rows.title: A free apartment comes with strings attached for Denver RV dwellers — and no place to park
rows.standfirst: Some people living in large vehicles face a stark choice: Move into an apartment offered by All In Mile High and leave their vehicle or continue risking fines, fees, or arrest on the streets

rows.title: Colorado legislature declines to override Jared Polis’ veto of social media bill after House caves
rows.standfirst: The override effort failed when the House of Representatives laid over the motion to override the veto until May 9, which is after the legislative session ends

rows.title: The latest victim of Trump cuts? Beetles keeping an invasive plant at bay in Colorado.
rows.standfirst: A coalition using root-eating beetles to wage war on invasive leafy spurges has been cut off from its federal grant money, putting the program, and the Yampa River watershed, in jeopardy

rows.title: Greeley wants to be the next city to cash in on the Cache la Poudre River
rows.standfirst: Greeley is piecing together a plan to reconnect and restore the Poudre River by getating out of its way — and making it a recreation destination

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers, being watched across the country, scale back artificial intelligence law
rows.standfirst: Pushback from Gov. Polis led to the proposed changes to delay the law for one year and exempt businesses with fewer than 500 employees in the first 15 months. All companies using AI must abide by state anti-discrimination laws.

rows.title: Front Range home values dip in latest property tax assessments, signaling some relief for homeowners
rows.standfirst: The typical homeowner won’t see major spikes in their 2026 tax bills like they did after the last re-assessment two years ago, which led to several rounds of property tax cuts at the state level
